verifications.claim: Artemis II launched successfully at 6:35 p.m. EDT on April 1, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.' '6:36 PM / April 1, 2026 Artemis II lifts off'; R4: 'lifted off from Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 6:35 p.m. ET.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm the exact time and date of successful launch.

verifications.claim: Artemis II launched from Pad 39B, Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Pad 39B'; 'Kennedy Space Center in Florida'; R2: 'Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center'; R4: 'Launch Pad 39B at the Kennedy Space Center'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources explicitly state the launch location as Pad 39B at Kennedy Space Center, Florida.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed moon mission in over 50 years.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since the end of the Apollo program 53 years ago'; R2: 'more than 50 years since we've headed toward the moon'; R4: 'first crewed flight around the moon in more than 50 years'; R5: 'first time since the 1960s and 70s'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe it as the first crewed lunar mission since Apollo, over 50 years ago.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of four astronauts.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: All sources: 'four astronauts'; 'The four astronauts'; 'four-person crew'
verifications.reasoning: Every reference explicitly states the crew has four astronauts.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission duration is 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'The 10-day mission'; R3: 'approximately 10-day test flight'; R4: '10-day journey'; R6: '10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: Most sources directly call it a 10-day mission; R1 notes 'nine and a half days' but context supports approximation.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is to test the Orion spacecraft systems before a future landing mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'thoroughly test their Orion capsule... making sure the ship's communications, navigation, propulsion and life support systems are working properly before heading to the moon'; R3: 'thorough checkout of Orion’s systems'; R4: 'test how Orion handles'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm testing Orion systems as primary goal prior to future missions.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a crewed flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'loop around it'; R3: 'lunar flyby'; R4: 'fly by the moon'; R5: 'lunar fly-by'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe the mission as a crewed lunar flyby without landing or orbit.

verifications.claim: Artemis III (Moon Landing) is planned for 2027.
verifications.label: AMBIGUOUS
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Artemis III mission by mid-2027... demonstrate key technology... Artemis IV mission' (landing in IV); R5: 'Artemis III, in 2027... Artemis IV finally flies' (landing in IV); R6: 'moon landing... during Artemis III... in 2027'
verifications.reasoning: Sources contradict: some plan Artemis III landing in 2027, others as test with landing in Artemis IV.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: All sources list exactly: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'
verifications.reasoning: All references precisely match the crew names and affiliations.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will orbit the moon.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'will not land on the moon or even go into lunar orbit. Instead, the plan is to loop around it'; R3: 'swing around the far side'; R5: 'did not land on the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state no lunar orbit, just a flyby.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will test the spacecraft's life support systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'communications, navigation, propulsion and life support systems'; R3: 'environmental control, life support systems... removes carbon dioxide... potable water dispenser... toilet'
verifications.reasoning: Sources directly confirm testing of life support systems.
